findings.title: Raw plaintext recovery codes sent to user storage
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the generatedCodes list as JSON and passes it to user.credentialManager().updateCredential, which hands it to every federated user storage provider supporting the type. These are the raw recovery codes, not hashed. External storages will therefore receive and likely persist plaintext recovery codes. The local provider stores only hashes, so this weakens the security model. The codes should be hashed before being sent, or the contract with providers should be documented explicitly.

findings.title: Removing a federated credential via removeStoredCredentialById is a no-op
findings.body: getCredential may now return a credential that lives in federated user storage. After a code is used, removeStoredCredentialById is called with that credential's ID, but that method only removes credentials from local storage. For federated credentials the removal does nothing. Also, nothing marks the used code as consumed in the federated store.

findings.title: Federated recovery codes never consumed, so the same code is reusable
findings.body: The bean builds a RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel from the credential returned by getCredential and takes the next unused code number from it. For federated credentials, nothing in the PR updates the 'used' state after a successful login, so the same code index is always requested. In the test storage, isValid also accepts any listed code, so a single code can be reused indefinitely.
